safety_boundary: Research evidence only. No financial advice, live trading, profitability claim, credentials, private exchange actions, or production-readiness claim.
obsolescence_triggers: new evidence on nonstationary validation or transaction-cost estimation
change to project execution, validation, or data-selection methodology

claims.text: Backtests must include explicit spread, fees, slippage and market-impact assumptions because implementation shortfall can materially differ from quoted-price returns.
Validation must treat market relationships as potentially time-varying and must report regime and sampling limits rather than assuming stable distributions.
Model validation requires independent challenge, outcome analysis, conceptual-soundness review and explicit limitations; a passing backtest alone is insufficient.

evidence.claim: Execution-quality research should compare decision or arrival prices with actual execution prices and identify explicit and implicit cost components.
evidence.title: Global Code of Conduct for the Foreign Exchange Market
evidence.applicability: FX execution governance and transaction-cost analysis concepts; useful as a control framework for research assumptions.
evidence.limitations: A conduct code does not provide universal cost coefficients and is not a crypto venue execution model.
obsolescence_triggers: material change in project execution benchmark

evidence.claim: Implementation shortfall separates paper returns from realized execution outcomes and provides a framework for measuring trading costs.
evidence.title: Implementation Shortfall: The Paper versus Reality
evidence.applicability: Benchmarking execution-cost assumptions in strategy backtests and post-trade research.
evidence.limitations: Predates electronic crypto markets and does not by itself estimate nonlinear impact or liquidation costs.

evidence.claim: Historical quoted spreads or fixed fee assumptions can understate realized costs when order size, volatility, queue position, fragmentation or liquidity stress changes.
evidence.title: The Economics of Trading Markets
evidence.applicability: Boundary-setting for interpreting simulated transaction costs across market types.
evidence.limitations: Reference work predates perpetual swaps and contemporary crypto fragmentation; parameterization requires current venue data.
obsolescence_triggers: change in target venues or order types

evidence.claim: Risk and validation processes should account for changing market conditions, stress periods and model limitations rather than relying only on recent average behavior.
evidence.title: Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
evidence.applicability: General model-risk controls for assumptions, changing environments, monitoring and outcomes analysis.
evidence.limitations: Bank supervisory guidance is not a direct prescription for crypto or FX alpha research and requires proportional adaptation.

evidence.claim: Predictive relationships and optimal models can change over time; model evaluation should consider structural change and adaptive behavior.
evidence.title: The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis
evidence.applicability: Conceptual basis for regime-aware evaluation and limited extrapolation of historical findings.
evidence.limitations: Broad hypothesis does not identify a unique regime detector or guarantee improved forecasts.
obsolescence_triggers: new comparative evidence on regime validation

evidence.claim: Regime segmentation can itself overfit data, create hindsight labels and reduce effective sample size; nonstationarity controls must be validated rather than assumed beneficial.
evidence.title: Forecasting in the Presence of Structural Breaks and Model Uncertainty
evidence.applicability: Opposing evidence and caution for structural-break and regime-conditioned forecasting.
evidence.limitations: Macroeconomic forecasting context differs from high-frequency crypto and FX execution data.
obsolescence_triggers: new evidence on online break detection

evidence.claim: Effective validation includes conceptual soundness, ongoing monitoring and outcomes analysis, with independent challenge and documented limitations.
evidence.title: Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
evidence.applicability: Research governance template for model inventory, validation evidence and limitation tracking.
evidence.limitations: Supervisory expectations for banks exceed and differ from a research repository; use as evidence, not production certification.

evidence.claim: Multiple model searches require adjusted evaluation because the best observed result can arise from selection bias rather than stable predictive ability.
evidence.title: A Test for Superior Predictive Ability
evidence.applicability: Benchmark-relative validation when many candidate models or rules are compared.
evidence.limitations: Test design, benchmark choice and dependence assumptions remain consequential; statistical superiority does not establish implementation viability.

evidence.claim: Cross-validation and holdout results can still be optimistic when preprocessing, feature selection or repeated experimentation leaks information across evaluation boundaries.
evidence.title: Leakage in Data Mining: Formulation, Detection, and Avoidance
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Kaufman, Shachar; Rosset, Saharon; Perlich, Claudia; Stitelman, Ori
evidence.applicability: Failure-mode evidence for research pipelines, feature generation and model-selection validation.
evidence.limitations: General data-mining evidence; financial time dependence and execution costs require additional controls.
